 002: """
 003: Basic Python Lebwohl-Lasher code.  Based on the paper 
 004: P.A. Lebwohl and G. Lasher, Phys. Rev. A, 6, 426-429 (1972).
 005: This version in 2D.
 006: 
 007: Run at the command line by typing:
 008: 
 009: python LebwohlLasher.py <ITERATIONS> <SIZE> <TEMPERATURE> <PLOTFLAG>
 010: 
 011: where:
 012:   ITERATIONS = number of Monte Carlo steps, where 1MCS is when each cell
 013:       has attempted a change once on average (i.e. SIZE*SIZE attempts)
 014:   SIZE = side length of square lattice
 015:   TEMPERATURE = reduced temperature in range 0.0 - 2.0.
 016:   PLOTFLAG = 0 for no plot, 1 for energy plot and 2 for angle plot.
 017:   
 018: The initial configuration is set at random. The boundaries
 019: are periodic throughout the simulation.  During the
 020: time-stepping, an array containing two domains is used; these
 021: domains alternate between old data and new data.

 224: def MC_step(arr,Ts,nmax):
 225:     """
 226:     Arguments:
 227: 	  arr (float(nmax,nmax)) = array that contains lattice data;
 228: 	  Ts (float) = reduced temperature (range 0 to 2);
 229:       nmax (int) = side length of square lattice.
 230:     Description:
 231:       Function to perform one MC step, which consists of an average
 232:       of 1 attempted change per lattice site.  Working with reduced
 233:       temperature Ts = kT/epsilon.  Function returns the acceptance
 234:       ratio for information.  This is the fraction of attempted changes
 235:       that are successful.  Generally aim to keep this around 0.5 for
 236:       efficient simulation.
 237: 	Returns:
 238: 	  accept/(nmax**2) (float) = acceptance ratio for current MCS.
 239:     """
 240:     #
 241:     # Pre-compute some random numbers.  This is faster than
 242:     # using lots of individual calls.  "scale" sets the width
 243:     # of the distribution for the angle changes - increases
 244:     # with temperature.
 245:     scale=0.1+Ts
 246:     accept = 0
 247:     xran = np.random.randint(0,high=nmax, size=(nmax,nmax))
 248:     yran = np.random.randint(0,high=nmax, size=(nmax,nmax))
 249:     aran = np.random.normal(scale=scale, size=(nmax,nmax))
 250:     for i in range(nmax):
 251:         for j in range(nmax):
 252:             ix = xran[i,j]
 253:             iy = yran[i,j]
 254:             ang = aran[i,j]
 255:             en0 = one_energy(arr,ix,iy,nmax)
 256:             arr[ix,iy] += ang
 257:             en1 = one_energy(arr,ix,iy,nmax)
 258:             if en1<=en0:
 259:                 accept += 1
 260:             else:
 261:             # Now apply the Monte Carlo test - compare
 262:             # exp( -(E_new - E_old) / T* ) >= rand(0,1)
 263:                 boltz = np.exp( -(en1 - en0) / Ts )
 264: 
 265:                 if boltz >= np.random.uniform(0.0,1.0):
 266:                     accept += 1
 267:                 else:
 268:                     arr[ix,iy] -= ang
 269:     return accept/(nmax*nmax)
 270: '''
